data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">With over two decades of coaching experience, Kelly Findley took over the Liberty men's soccer program in December of 2018.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Known for player development, Findley has compiled a 164-144-44 record and led two teams to the NCAA Tournament during head coaching stints at Liberty, Mars Hill (1999-00), Butler (2006-10) and NC State (2011-16).\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">After seeing the 2020 season moved to the Spring of 2021, the Flames posted a 7-3-2 mark in Findley’s second year in Lynchburg. For the first time in program history, Liberty received a national ranking during the year, climbing as high as 15\u003Csup>th\u003C/sup> in the United Soccer Coaches Poll on March 15.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">The Flames opened the season with a program-record six consecutive shutouts, including the program’s first-ever win at North Carolina. Liberty went on to finish the year with eight shutouts to post the second-best shutout percentage in the nation (.667).\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Off the field, the program has made its mark academically during Findley’s two seasons. The Flames posted the highest team GPA of any Liberty male sport with a 3.55 GPA during the 2020-21 season. The men’s soccer program had 24 of its 27 student-athletes post a 3.0 or better for the academic year.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Meanwhile, during a challenging and unique year due to COVID-19, the Flames had 28 of their 30 student-athletes or 93% of its roster post a 3.0 or better for the 2019-21 academic year. The Flames posted the highest GPA of any Liberty men's team during the spring semester.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">In addition, senior midfielder Ruben Garcia was named to the 2019 CoSIDA Academic All-America Division I men's soccer team in program history, becoming only the third player in program history to garner selection to the prestigious squad. Garcia also was named the 2019 ASUN Men's Scholar Athlete of the Year.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Findley came to Liberty after serving as the associate head coach at Davidson during the 2018 season and a one-year term with the Sporting Kansas City Development Academy in 2017.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">During his time as head coach at NC State, Findley had three nationally ranked recruiting classes, including the No. 3 ranked class by TopDrawerSoccer.com in 2014.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">The Wolfpack spent multiple weeks ranked in the national polls during several different seasons. NC State was ranked during a six-week stretch in 2015, climbing as high as No. 20 in the polls, while his team was ranked as high as No. 14 in 2012.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Findley's ability to develop young talent established his program as a launching pad to the professional ranks. In 2014, Clement Simonin was the No. 9 overall pick in the MLS SuperDraft by Toronto FC and Conor Donovan was the No. 22 overall pick by the Orlando City SC. Additionally, Alex Martinez was selected in the third round of the draft in 2013.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Prior to his days in Raleigh, Findley posted a winning record during four of his five seasons as the head coach at Butler. With the Bulldogs, Findley posted a record of 59-25-15 overall and 24-7-8 in Horizon League conference play. He was named the Horizon League Coach of the Year in both 2009 and 2010, after guiding Butler to the NCAA Tournament both seasons.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">His 2010 Butler squad entered the NCAA Tournament ranked No. 5 nationally and was one of only two unbeaten teams in the nation. The squad finished the year 16-1-3. He also mentored the Horizon League Player of the Year and Herman Trophy semifinalist Ben Sippola and two-time Horizon League Defender of the Year Matt Hedges.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Sippola and Hedges were named to the NSCAA All-America first team and later drafted by MLS teams. Sippola was taken by the Columbus Crew in the 2011 MLS Supplemental Draft and went on to play for the Crew. Later, he played professionally in Sweden and New Zealand.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp>Hedges, who was the 11\u003Csup>th\u003C/sup> pick in the 2012 MLS SuperDraft, became the all-time leader in MLS appearances for FC Dallas in 2020. The 2016 MLS Defender of the Year, he was selected to the MLS Best IX in 2015 and 2016 and has been a MLS All-Star three times. He has also seen National Team caps.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">The 2009 squad also won the Horizon League championship, and over his final three years at Butler went 18-1-5 in conference play.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Findley spent five seasons at Charlotte, serving as an assistant coach (2001-03) and associate head coach (2004-05).\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">During his tenure at Charlotte, the 49ers compiled a 42-40-14 record, including an 11-7-1 mark in 2004. During his third season at Charlotte, the 49ers reached the finals of the Conference USA Tournament for only the second time in school history, losing the title game on penalty kicks.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Findley jumpstarted his head coaching career at Mars Hill College where he led the program during the 1999 and 2000 seasons. He guided the Lions to a 17-22 mark over the two seasons, including a 10-8 overall record and a runner-up finish in the South Atlantic Conference in 2000.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Findley also spent one season as an assistant coach at Miami (Ohio) University (1998), two seasons as an assistant coach with the Charlotte Eagles professional soccer team (1996-97) and one season as an assistant coach at Judson College (1992). During his tenure with the Charlotte Eagles, the professional club won two South Atlantic Division Championships, made two playoff appearances and posted a national runner-up finish.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Findley was a four-time Most Valuable Player as an undergraduate on the men's soccer team at Judson University in Elgin, Ill. He graduated with a secondary education degree.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">He was a three-time NAIA All-American, a three-time NCCAA All-American and a two-time NSCAA All-American as a midfielder. He was named the Northern Illinois Intercollegiate Conference Player of the Year for three consecutive seasons, and he was named Judson's Athlete of the Year in 1990.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Findley helped Judson to its first NCCAA National Tournament championship in 1991, and he finished his collegiate career in fifth place on Judson's all-time assist chart with 48 career assists.  He was named to Judson's Athletic Hall of Fame in 2005.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">Following his collegiate career, Findley played professional soccer with the Charlotte Eagles for six seasons. He helped the Eagles to three South Atlantic Division Championships, five divisional playoff appearances and two trips to the national finals.\u003C/p>\r\n\r\n\u003Cp data-mce-style=\"font-family: Verdana, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #000000;\">A former North Carolina ODP State Team coach, Findley holds a USSF \"A\" license and an NSCAA Premier Diploma.  He and his wife, Joanne and children Gabe, Elysia, Corinne, Stephen and Keane live in Glodi Konga joined the Liberty men’s soccer coaching staff in July of 2025 as an associate head coach. The former Flame will assist in all aspects of the Liberty program.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHe returns to Liberty after two years as the inaugural men’s head coach at New College of Florida in Sarasota, Fla., where he led the Mighty Bayans to a 10-3-1 record in the program’s first season (2023).\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nPrior to his role at NCF, Konga was a member of the Eastern University coaching staff from 2021 to 2023. He began as an assistant coach, served as interim head coach in 2022, and was promoted to full-time head coach in 2023.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nKonga also served as head coach at Valley Forge for the 2017 and 2018 seasons. During his tenure, he was an Assistant Professor and Program Director of Sport Management.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nWith more than a decade of coaching experience, Konga currently serves as Director of Soccer for Central Virginia United Soccer Club. He has served as head coach with Buxmont Torch FC (NPSL) and was part of the technical staff with Sarasota Paradise (USL2), helping the team win two divisional titles on the road to becoming a professional club.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nAs a player, Konga was a defender for Liberty in 2014 and 2015, appearing in 18 games with 14 starts. In 2014, he helped anchor a defense that recorded six shutouts, contributing to an 11-6-1 season. A native of London, England, Konga transferred to Liberty from Cairn University (2012–2013) after beginning his collegiate career at Cloud County (2011–2012). He was part of Cloud County’s 2011 NJCAA National Championship team, which posted a 22-1-3 record with 17 shutouts, and he has since been inducted into the school’s Hall of Fame.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nFollowing graduation, Konga played professionally for the Philadelphia Fury for two seasons.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nKonga earned his bachelor’s degree in exercise science (2015) and master’s degree in sport management (2016) from Liberty. He completed his Ph.D. in Sports Leadership at Concordia University Chicago in 2023. He holds a UEFA “B” License and has led several teams on international tours with Athletes in Action and Ambassadors Football, competing against professional teams.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nHe and his wife, Arianna, have a two-year-old son, Salehi joined the Flames men's soccer staff as an assistant coach in July of 2025.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nA 20-year high school and club coaching veteran, Salehi comes to Liberty after two years as the head coach of the Fossil Ridge girls’ soccer team in Fort Collins, Colo. Under his guidance, the Sabercats posted a 28-6-3 record and won the school’s first 5A State Championship in 2025.\u003Cbr />\r\nBefore Fossil Ridge, Salehi led the Liberty Common School men’s program in Fort Collins for eight seasons. He led the Eagles to a 133-31-9 record and first-place league finishes in the 3A Patriot League each season of his tenure. In 2017, he led Liberty Common to a state championship.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nDuring his 10 years of coaching in the Fort Collins area, Salehi’s teams posted a combined record of 161-37-6, played in state six semifinal and three state championship games and won two state titles.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nSalehi also coached on the club level, working with Colorado Rapids Academy and Arsenal Colorado. This past spring, he and former Liberty men’s soccer associate head coach Jake Berry coached the UPSL Lynchburg FC team to a first-place finish in the DMV-B Division and won the DMV Regional Championship.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nSalehi began his coaching career at Sonoma State in 1995. He also played soccer during his time at the school. He earned his bachelor’s degree in psychology from Sonoma State in 1995.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nSalehi and his wife, Becky, have three children. Ashley, Allison and Josh. Allison is currently the strength and conditioning coach for the Liberty Men’s Club Hockey team and the Women’s Performance Dance team. Josh is currently pursuing a master’s degree at Liberty and serves as a manager for the Flames men’s soccer team.\u003Cbr
